clue.text: Soldier has location for drone?

blocks.note: a para is a paratrooper
a site is a location

explanation.surface: A soldier is assigned a base from which to launch a drone aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drone' suggests the military aircraft, which fits the soldier, but here it is the idle person living off others; the question mark flags that sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A drone is someone who lives on the efforts of others without contributing, just as a parasite does.

clue.text: Discipline press covering Northern Ireland

indicators.note: something covering another wraps round it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: to press is to push
NI is the standard abbreviation for Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: The newspapers are reporting on a disciplinary matter in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' reads as the newspapers, but it is the verb meaning push.
explanation.definitionFit: To discipline someone, as a verb, is to impose a penalty on them for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Curiosity of artist right before thing with unknown

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
R is the abbreviation for right
'it' stands for a thing
in algebra x, y and z are unknowns

explanation.surface: An artist's quirky interest leads to work involving some mysterious object.
explanation.walkthrough: Four small pieces in a row; RA (Royal Academician) and Y for an algebraic unknown are standard crossword shorthand.
explanation.definitionFit: A curiosity is an unusual, seldom-seen object that people find interesting, which is what a rarity is.

clue.text: See zebra drunk on drug cocktail

indicators.note: something drunk staggers about out of order, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
E is ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: An absurd scene: a zebra intoxicated after taking drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: All the letters, including the E for ecstasy, are mixed together; 'drunk' doubles as a nod to the cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a well-known mixed drink of vodka with cranberry and grapefruit juice, served as a long cocktail.

clue.text: Russian mint possibly, after time, finds agitator

indicators.note: coming after something means following it, so the piece named first in the clue goes second in the answer

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
a Russian mint would make roubles, the Russian currency; 'possibly' marks this as a playful description

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a political agitator connected to the Russian state mint.
explanation.walkthrough: The mint is not a herb or sweet but the place that makes coins, so a Russian one makes roubles; it comes after T.
explanation.definitionFit: An agitator stirs up unrest and causes difficulties for others, the essence of someone who deliberately creates strife.

clue.text: Passive join in petition

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits within it

blocks.note: to sue is to petition, as in a court or to sue for peace
to pin things is to join them together

explanation.surface: A meek person signs up to a petition without doing anything more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Petition' is the verb here: to sue for something is to petition for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Supine figuratively describes someone who is weakly inactive and failing to resist, so it matches passive.

clue.text: Heads of ultra socialist union revoke parliament to take over

indicators.note: the head of each word is its opening letter, so only those are kept

blocks.note: the initial letters of these five words

explanation.surface: Leaders of a hard-left union plan to abolish parliament and seize control.
explanation.walkthrough: The political surface hides a simple pick of first letters, and the definition sits neatly in the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: To usurp is to seize power or a position wrongfully, a forcible seizing of control from others.

clue.text: Absolute little devil sanctioned

blocks.note: an imp is a small mischievous devil
licit means lawful or permitted

explanation.surface: A mischievous little rascal has been officially approved without question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Absolute' fits the sense in 'implicit trust' or 'implicit faith', meaning unqualified.
explanation.definitionFit: Implicit can mean wholehearted and without reservation, as in complete unquestioning faith, a sense shared with absolute.

clue.text: Balanced on ring taking part in equestrian competition

blocks.note: balanced means even
a ting is a ringing sound

explanation.surface: A rider keeps steady in the ring during a horse show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' suggests the show ring, but it is a bell-like sound; in a down clue, 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the horse-riding sport combining dressage, cross-country and show jumping; the verb form means competing in it.

clue.text: Rant and roar about storyteller

indicators.note: letters moved about are rearranged into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone shouts and bellows complaints about the person telling the story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' reads as 'concerning', but it is the instruction to mix up the eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrator is the person who recounts the events of a tale, so is a teller of stories.

clue.text: Crease the French found on rear

blocks.note: the rump is the rear end
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A crease in French trousers turns up on the seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found on' places the French article after the rear in this across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To crease fabric is to crumple or wrinkle it untidily, which is exactly what this verb means.

clue.text: Renovated college's pink instrument

indicators.note: something renovated has been rebuilt and remade, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written, including the S

explanation.surface: A college has had its musical instrument refurbished and painted pink.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive S belongs in the fodder; all twelve letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a percussion device with tuned metal bars struck by hammers, played in orchestras and bands.

clue.text: Seductive spirit modelled with Lycra regularly

indicators.note: at regular intervals means every other letter is kept

blocks.note: an artist's model sits, so modelled is sat
the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: A sultry figure posed for a picture wearing stretchy Lycra.
explanation.walkthrough: To model for an artist is to sit, so 'modelled' gives SAT. Lycra is a stretchy fabric used in sportswear.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a satyr is a lustful woodland deity, half man and half goat, given to pursuing nymphs.

clue.text: Dance position for writer

blocks.note: a ball is a formal dance
a point is a position or place

explanation.surface: A dancer's stance is described for an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' looks like a person, but here it is the thing you write with.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer can be any implement used for writing, and this ink pen with a tiny rolling tip is one.

clue.text: Consequence of engineers getting instruments

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
percussion is the collective name for drums and other struck instruments

explanation.surface: An outcome follows when engineers are issued with new tools.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers; 'instruments' is musical rather than technical.
explanation.definitionFit: A repercussion is an effect or result, often unwelcome, that follows from an action, so it means consequence.

clue.text: Nimble Tory left embraced by agent

indicators.note: something embraced is held inside another's arms, so it goes within

blocks.note: a spy is a secret agent
the Tories are the political right
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: An agile Conservative politician has defected and been taken in by a spy.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory and left look like opposites in politics, but here both just supply pieces that go inside the agent. Tory is the everyday name for Britain's Conservatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprightly means lively and full of energy in movement, much like being quick and light on one's feet.

clue.text: I rip both apart in bar

indicators.note: something pulled apart is broken up and can be reassembled in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A brawler boasts of tearing two people to pieces in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like the pub where the fight happens, but it is the verb meaning forbid.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar something is to forbid or ban it formally, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Situation where big cat eats round another feline

indicators.note: what is eaten goes inside the eater

blocks.note: a lion is a big cat
O is round in shape
a cat is a feline

explanation.surface: A grim scene in which a lion devours another member of the cat family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' is not a preposition here: it supplies an O, which goes in with the second cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation, in the sense of where something is sited, is its place or position, which is what a location is.

clue.text: I adore joiner travelling to state capital

indicators.note: things travelling are on the move and shifting position, so the letters change places

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone declares their love for a carpenter who is heading off to a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: A joiner is a woodworker; the city is the capital of the Brazilian state with the same name, so 'state capital' is fair even though Brasília is the national capital.
explanation.definitionFit: This Brazilian city is the seat of government of the state named after it, and was once the national seat too.

clue.text: Expedition partially explores a far island

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used, so a run of consecutive letters is taken

blocks.note: runs from the end of the first word across the next two into the last

explanation.surface: An exploration party visits part of a distant island.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans four words; the surface fits the definition, so a solver may look for a synonym before spotting the run of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari is an overland journey or trip, especially in Africa, to observe or hunt wild animals.

clue.text: Disrupted recent focus

indicators.note: something disrupted is thrown into disorder, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's attention has lately been broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recent' looks like a description, but it is the six letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The focus of something is its central point of interest or activity, the hub around which it turns.

clue.text: Male to deal with what's found on top

blocks.note: he is the male pronoun
to address a problem is to deal with it

explanation.surface: A man is tasked with handling whatever comes out on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's found on top' sounds like a winner, but it means something worn on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative covering such as a feathered bonnet or tiara is worn on the head, at the very top of a person.

clue.text: Dig love regularly entering river

indicators.note: at regular intervals means every other letter is kept
to enter is to go inside, so one piece is put within another

blocks.note: the first and third letters
the Dee is a river in Britain

explanation.surface: A gardener tends lovingly to the riverbank, often turning over the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a river in Scotland and another in Wales and England, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: To delve is to excavate or turn over earth with a spade, an old sense now mostly figurative for researching.

clue.text: Look across river and ruminate

indicators.note: to lie across something is to straddle it, so one piece spans another

blocks.note: to gaze is to look
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone stares out over the river, lost in thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruminate' looks like pondering, which fits the gazing picture, but it is the cow's sense of chewing grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruminant animals such as cattle feed on grass in a field, and ruminate can mean to chew the cud.

clue.text: Check person tying knot around end of sail

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter
to go around something is to enclose it

blocks.note: to tie the knot is to marry, so this person is getting married
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A sailor inspects someone fastening a knot round the corner of a sail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tying knot' sounds nautical alongside the sail, but tying the knot is the idiom for getting married.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to restrain or curb it, as a rider does with the headgear and reins on a horse.

clue.text: Amuse detective inspectors with booklet

blocks.note: DI is a detective inspector, so DIs are several
a tract is a short pamphlet

explanation.surface: Police officers are entertained by a little pamphlet.
explanation.walkthrough: DI is the British police rank of Detective Inspector; a tract is a small pamphlet, often religious or political.
explanation.definitionFit: To amuse someone can mean to divert or occupy their attention, drawing it away from other matters.

clue.text: Can King and Queen potter?

blocks.note: a tin is a can
K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A question about whether the royal couple are able to make pottery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like the verb opening a question and 'potter' like a ceramicist, but one is a tin and the other a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To potter is to occupy oneself in a leisurely way with small jobs, much like fiddling about at repairs.

clue.text: Break toy with returning issue

indicators.note: something returning comes back the way it went, so its letters run backwards

blocks.note: to toy with something is to play with it
to issue is to emit

explanation.surface: A child snaps a plaything that keeps coming back with a fault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break' looks like a verb about damaging the toy, but it is the noun for a school pause.
explanation.definitionFit: At school, a break is the short recess between lessons when pupils go outside to have fun.
